If you have any questions regarding the entrance requirements and equivalents, please contact Program Advising . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you\u2019ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 \u2013 English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT\u2019s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor\u2019s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor\u2019s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. content.text:
Before applying to the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements

1. **Complete the pre-entry assessment first**
   - Contact the program area for an evaluation of your work experience, any required pre-entry courses, and approval of your Proposed Program of Study.
   - Upload the completed pre-entry assessment with your application.
   - Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree matrix can count toward the degree.

2. **Meet the English requirement**
   - **Category 2 English language proficiency**, such as English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent.

3. **Meet one of these entry options** — you choose **one**:
   - A BCIT Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology diploma with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma from a nationally accredited, related engineering technology program with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma average between **60% and 65%**, followed by three of these four courses with an overall average of at least **70%**:
     - **ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**
     - **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**
     - **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**
     - **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**
   - Equivalent post-secondary education and registration—or eligibility to register—as an Applied Science Technologist.

### Application preparation

- Include proof that you meet the entrance requirements.
- Convert transcripts and supporting documents to PDF.
- Have a credit card ready for the application fee.
- Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but intakes may fill before their deadlines. Applying early is recommended.
- The program uses a first-qualified process while space remains.

### If you studied outside Canada

You may need a comprehensive **ICES** credential evaluation, including course-by-course results and GPA calculations. International students also require a valid BCIT study permit before starting. The program’s stored information indicates that graduates may apply for a post-graduation work permit, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements and final IRCC approval.

The program is **part-time, in person, at the Burnaby campus**, with classes generally scheduled in the evenings or on weekends.

[Review the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).

response.answer:
Yes, the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics** is available to international applicants.

Key points:

- You must complete the program’s **pre-entry assessment** and meet the English and academic entrance requirements.
- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, you will generally need a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation** with course-by-course results and GPA calculations. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- A valid **BCIT study permit is required before starting the program**.
- The program is part-time and delivered in person at the Burnaby campus.
- To graduate, students must complete the mandatory ELEX 8300 — Industry Project and have at least **two years of relevant work experience before graduation**.
- Graduates may apply for a **post-graduation work permit**, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements. Final approval is determined by IRCC.

International application deadlines are earlier than domestic deadlines and may vary by intake. Intakes can fill before the deadline, so applying early is recommended.

[View the program’s international applicant and entrance information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)

rule_sets.name: Electronics BTech admission
rule_sets.notes: Find out more about getting started in the program! If the Bachelor of Technology in Electronics program interests you, review the entrance requirements below. If you have any questions regarding the entrance requirements and equivalents, please contact Program Advising . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Courses

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Technology in Electronics is a baccalaureate degree designed for electronics technologists (or equivalent) who wish to complete a degree while working and gain skills for job promotion. The program provides graduates with the knowledge and skills required to design electrical, computer, automation and communication systems. Delivery: in person. See details . About the program The program is approved by the BC Provincial Ministry of Advanced Education. It develops strong mathematics, physics and analytical foundations and broadens this skill set by including business management and liberal studies elements. This degree enhances career advancement opportunities for graduates and supplies the high technology sector with well educated professionals possessing strong practical skills. For projected BTech Electronics course offering information, please view the Course Plan [PDF] and the sample Program Plan [PDF] . You can also take a look at our tentative Fall 202630 Timetable [PDF] . Who it’s for This BCIT Flexible Learning (formerly Part-time Studies) program is scheduled to serve the needs of working professionals who wish to continue their education while working. BCIT Flexible Learning classes are offered year-round, three terms per year, on evenings or weekends. What grads can do B.Tech Electronics graduates have a wide range of career opportunities. They can work as technical design engineers, engineering managers, or professional engineers. They may also join engineering consultancies, pursue careers in sales and marketing, work for the government, become technology entrepreneurs, or further their education with advanced degrees in engineering or business management. Next up Entrance Requirements

content.text:
Yes, the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics** is available to international applicants.

Key points:

- You must complete the program’s **pre-entry assessment** and meet the English and academic entrance requirements.
- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, you will generally need a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation** with course-by-course results and GPA calculations. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- A valid **BCIT study permit is required before starting the program**.
- The program is part-time and delivered in person at the Burnaby campus.
- To graduate, students must complete the mandatory industry project and have at least **two years of relevant work experience before graduation**.
- Graduates may apply for a **post-graduation work permit**, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements. Final approval is determined by IRCC.

International application deadlines are earlier than domestic deadlines and may vary by intake. Intakes can fill before the deadline, so applying early is recommended.

[View the program’s international applicant and entrance information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)

rule_sets.name: Electronics BTech admission
rule_sets.notes: Find out more about getting started in the program! If the Bachelor of Technology in Electronics program interests you, review the entrance requirements below. If you have any questions regarding the entrance requirements and equivalents, please contact Program Advising . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Courses

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Technology in Electronics is a baccalaureate degree designed for electronics technologists (or equivalent) who wish to complete a degree while working and gain skills for job promotion. The program provides graduates with the knowledge and skills required to design electrical, computer, automation and communication systems. Delivery: in person. See details . About the program The program is approved by the BC Provincial Ministry of Advanced Education. It develops strong mathematics, physics and analytical foundations and broadens this skill set by including business management and liberal studies elements. This degree enhances career advancement opportunities for graduates and supplies the high technology sector with well educated professionals possessing strong practical skills. For projected BTech Electronics course offering information, please view the Course Plan [PDF] and the sample Program Plan [PDF] . You can also take a look at our tentative Fall 202630 Timetable [PDF] . Who it’s for This BCIT Flexible Learning (formerly Part-time Studies) program is scheduled to serve the needs of working professionals who wish to continue their education while working. BCIT Flexible Learning classes are offered year-round, three terms per year, on evenings or weekends. What grads can do B.Tech Electronics graduates have a wide range of career opportunities. They can work as technical design engineers, engineering managers, or professional engineers. They may also join engineering consultancies, pursue careers in sales and marketing, work for the government, become technology entrepreneurs, or further their education with advanced degrees in engineering or business management. conversation.content: Is it online or in person?

It is **in person** at BCIT’s **Burnaby campus**. The program is part-time through Flexible Learning, with classes offered in the evenings or on weekends.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)
Is it full-time or part-time?

It is **part-time**, offered through **Flexible Learning**. Classes are scheduled year-round, typically in the evenings or on weekends.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements

1. **Complete the pre-entry assessment first**
   - Contact the program area for an evaluation of your work experience, any required pre-entry courses, and approval of your Proposed Program of Study.
   - Upload the completed pre-entry assessment with your application.
   - Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree matrix can count toward the degree.

2. **Meet the English requirement**
   - **Category 2 English language proficiency**, such as English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent.

3. **Meet one of these entry options** — you choose **one**:
   - A BCIT Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology diploma with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma from a nationally accredited, related engineering technology program with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma average between **60% and 65%**, followed by three of these four courses with an overall average of at least **70%**:
     - **ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**
     - **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**
     - **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**
     - **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**
   - Equivalent post-secondary education and registration—or eligibility to register—as an Applied Science Technologist.

### Application preparation

- Include proof that you meet the entrance requirements.
- Convert transcripts and supporting documents to PDF.
- Have a credit card ready for the application fee.
- Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but intakes may fill before their deadlines. Applying early is recommended.
- The program uses a first-qualified process while space remains.

### If you studied outside Canada

You may need a comprehensive **ICES** credential evaluation, including course-by-course results and GPA calculations. International students also require a valid BCIT study permit before starting. The program’s stored information indicates that graduates may apply for a post-graduation work permit, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements and final IRCC approval.

The program is **part-time, in person, at the Burnaby campus**, with classes generally scheduled in the evenings or on weekends.

[Review the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).
What about international applicants?

Yes, the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics** is available to international applicants.

Key points:

- You must complete the program’s **pre-entry assessment** and meet the English and academic entrance requirements.
- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, you will generally need a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation** with course-by-course results and GPA calculations. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- A valid **BCIT study permit is required before starting the program**.
- The program is part-time and delivered in person at the Burnaby campus.
- To graduate, students must complete the mandatory ELEX 8300 — Industry Project and have at least **two years of relevant work experience before graduation**.
- Graduates may apply for a **post-graduation work permit**, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements. Final approval is determined by IRCC.

International application deadlines are earlier than domestic deadlines and may vary by intake. Intakes can fill before the deadline, so applying early is recommended.

[View the program’s international applicant and entrance information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the listed entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**.

For the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, applicants must complete the pre-entry assessment, meet the English requirement, and satisfy **one** entry option. Qualified applicants are accepted on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**, so intakes may fill before the deadline.

For international applicants, a valid BCIT study permit is also required before starting. Confirm your situation with BCIT Program Advising.

[Review the program’s admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

- **Pre-entry assessment:** The program area must evaluate your work experience, identify any required pre-entry courses, and approve your Proposed Program of Study.
- **English equivalency:** Whether your English qualification meets **Category 2 — English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**.
- **Entry-option equivalency:** Whether your diploma is considered a related, nationally accredited engineering technology credential and whether your course average qualifies.
- **The 60–65% diploma-average route:** Whether your results satisfy the requirement to complete three of the four specified courses—**ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**, **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**, **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**, and **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**—with an overall average of at least 70%.
- **Equivalent education or professional registration:** Whether your education and **ASTTBC** registration, or eligibility to register, satisfy the fourth entry option.
- **International credential evaluation:** Whether an ICES report is required in your circumstances and whether an evaluation from another Canadian service will be accepted.
- **Study permit and international enrolment details:** The program record requires a valid BCIT study permit before starting, but the international source evidence does not publish a definitive study-permit status. Confirm this directly with BCIT.
- **Admission and space:** Meeting the requirements does not guarantee admission; acceptance is first-qualified while space remains, and intakes may fill early.
- **Post-graduation work permit:** The program record says graduates may apply, but final eligibility and approval must be confirmed with **IRCC**.

rule_sets.name: Electronics BTech admission
rule_sets.notes: Find out more about getting started in the program! If the Bachelor of Technology in Electronics program interests you, review the entrance requirements below. If you have any questions regarding the entrance requirements and equivalents, please contact Program Advising . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Courses

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Technology in Electronics is a baccalaureate degree designed for electronics technologists (or equivalent) who wish to complete a degree while working and gain skills for job promotion. The program provides graduates with the knowledge and skills required to design electrical, computer, automation and communication systems. Delivery: in person. See details . About the program The program is approved by the BC Provincial Ministry of Advanced Education. It develops strong mathematics, physics and analytical foundations and broadens this skill set by including business management and liberal studies elements. This degree enhances career advancement opportunities for graduates and supplies the high technology sector with well educated professionals possessing strong practical skills. For projected BTech Electronics course offering information, please view the Course Plan [PDF] and the sample Program Plan [PDF] . You can also take a look at our tentative Fall 202630 Timetable [PDF] . Who it’s for This BCIT Flexible Learning (formerly Part-time Studies) program is scheduled to serve the needs of working professionals who wish to continue their education while working. BCIT Flexible Learning classes are offered year-round, three terms per year, on evenings or weekends. What grads can do B.Tech Electronics graduates have a wide range of career opportunities. They can work as technical design engineers, engineering managers, or professional engineers. They may also join engineering consultancies, pursue careers in sales and marketing, work for the government, become technology entrepreneurs, or further their education with advanced degrees in engineering or business management. Next up Entrance Requirements

conversation.content: Is it full-time or part-time?

It is **part-time**, offered through **Flexible Learning**. Classes are scheduled year-round, typically in the evenings or on weekends.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements

1. **Complete the pre-entry assessment first**
   - Contact the program area for an evaluation of your work experience, any required pre-entry courses, and approval of your Proposed Program of Study.
   - Upload the completed pre-entry assessment with your application.
   - Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree matrix can count toward the degree.

2. **Meet the English requirement**
   - **Category 2 English language proficiency**, such as English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent.

3. **Meet one of these entry options** — you choose **one**:
   - A BCIT Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology diploma with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma from a nationally accredited, related engineering technology program with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma average between **60% and 65%**, followed by three of these four courses with an overall average of at least **70%**:
     - **ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**
     - **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**
     - **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**
     - **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**
   - Equivalent post-secondary education and registration—or eligibility to register—as an Applied Science Technologist.

### Application preparation

- Include proof that you meet the entrance requirements.
- Convert transcripts and supporting documents to PDF.
- Have a credit card ready for the application fee.
- Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but intakes may fill before their deadlines. Applying early is recommended.
- The program uses a first-qualified process while space remains.

### If you studied outside Canada

You may need a comprehensive **ICES** credential evaluation, including course-by-course results and GPA calculations. International students also require a valid BCIT study permit before starting. The program’s stored information indicates that graduates may apply for a post-graduation work permit, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements and final IRCC approval.

The program is **part-time, in person, at the Burnaby campus**, with classes generally scheduled in the evenings or on weekends.

[Review the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).
What about international applicants?

Yes, the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics** is available to international applicants.

Key points:

- You must complete the program’s **pre-entry assessment** and meet the English and academic entrance requirements.
- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, you will generally need a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation** with course-by-course results and GPA calculations. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- A valid **BCIT study permit is required before starting the program**.
- The program is part-time and delivered in person at the Burnaby campus.
- To graduate, students must complete the mandatory ELEX 8300 — Industry Project and have at least **two years of relevant work experience before graduation**.
- Graduates may apply for a **post-graduation work permit**, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements. Final approval is determined by IRCC.

International application deadlines are earlier than domestic deadlines and may vary by intake. Intakes can fill before the deadline, so applying early is recommended.

[View the program’s international applicant and entrance information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)

No. Meeting the listed entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**.

For the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, applicants must complete the pre-entry assessment, meet the English requirement, and satisfy **one** entry option. Qualified applicants are accepted on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**, so intakes may fill before the deadline.

For international applicants, a valid BCIT study permit is also required before starting. Confirm your situation with BCIT Program Advising.

If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Technology in Electronics is a baccalaureate degree designed for electronics technologists (or equivalent) who wish to complete a degree while working and gain skills for job promotion. The program provides graduates with the knowledge and skills required to design electrical, computer, automation and communication systems. Delivery: in person. See details . About the program The program is approved by the BC Provincial Ministry of Advanced Education. It develops strong mathematics, physics and analytical foundations and broadens this skill set by including business management and liberal studies elements. This degree enhances career advancement opportunities for graduates and supplies the high technology sector with well educated professionals possessing strong practical skills. For projected BTech Electronics course offering information, please view the Course Plan [PDF] and the sample Program Plan [PDF] . You can also take a look at our tentative Fall 202630 Timetable [PDF] . Who it’s for This BCIT Flexible Learning (formerly Part-time Studies) program is scheduled to serve the needs of working professionals who wish to continue their education while working. BCIT Flexible Learning classes are offered year-round, three terms per year, on evenings or weekends. What grads can do B.Tech Electronics graduates have a wide range of career opportunities. They can work as technical design engineers, engineering managers, or professional engineers. They may also join engineering consultancies, pursue careers in sales and marketing, work for the government, become technology entrepreneurs, or further their education with advanced degrees in engineering or business management. Next up Entrance Requirements

Use the provided tools for every factual claim about courses, prerequisites, eligibility, or program progress. Never guess policy. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Be concise and clear. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. Clearly label any inference, or omit it. uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. Respond entirely in the language of the current student question: English. Conversation history may provide subject or entity context but must never determine or carry over the response language. Keep co-op work terms, practical-work hours, and academic level progression separate. Simply put, BCIT needs to confirm:

- Whether your **pre-entry assessment** is complete and whether you need any additional courses.
- Whether your English qualification meets the required standard.
- Whether your diploma qualifies under one of the entry options.
- If using the 60–65% diploma-average option, whether you meet the requirements involving three of these courses:
  - **ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**
  - **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**

- Whether your education and **ASTTBC** registration—or eligibility for registration—meet the fourth option.

- Whether space remains in the intake. Meeting the requirements does **not** guarantee admission.
- Whether you qualify for a post-graduation work permit; final approval comes from **IRCC**.

For confirmation, contact **BCIT Program Advising** and review the [program admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).

conversation.content: What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements

1. **Complete the pre-entry assessment first**
   - Contact the program area for an evaluation of your work experience, any required pre-entry courses, and approval of your Proposed Program of Study.
   - Upload the completed pre-entry assessment with your application.
   - Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree matrix can count toward the degree.

2. **Meet the English requirement**
   - **Category 2 English language proficiency**, such as English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent.

3. **Meet one of these entry options** — you choose **one**:
   - A BCIT Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology diploma with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma from a nationally accredited, related engineering technology program with a minimum **65% course average**.
   - A diploma average between **60% and 65%**, followed by three of these four courses with an overall average of at least **70%**:
     - **ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**
     - **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**
     - **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**
     - **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**
   - Equivalent post-secondary education and registration—or eligibility to register—as an Applied Science Technologist.

### Application preparation

- Include proof that you meet the entrance requirements.
- Convert transcripts and supporting documents to PDF.
- Have a credit card ready for the application fee.
- Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but intakes may fill before their deadlines. Applying early is recommended.
- The program uses a first-qualified process while space remains.

### If you studied outside Canada

You may need a comprehensive **ICES** credential evaluation, including course-by-course results and GPA calculations. International students also require a valid BCIT study permit before starting. The program’s stored information indicates that graduates may apply for a post-graduation work permit, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements and final IRCC approval.

The program is **part-time, in person, at the Burnaby campus**, with classes generally scheduled in the evenings or on weekends.

[Review the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).
What about international applicants?

Yes, the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics** is available to international applicants.

Key points:

- You must complete the program’s **pre-entry assessment** and meet the English and academic entrance requirements.
- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, you will generally need a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation** with course-by-course results and GPA calculations. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- A valid **BCIT study permit is required before starting the program**.
- The program is part-time and delivered in person at the Burnaby campus.
- To graduate, students must complete the mandatory ELEX 8300 — Industry Project and have at least **two years of relevant work experience before graduation**.
- Graduates may apply for a **post-graduation work permit**, subject to meeting all IRCC requirements. Final approval is determined by IRCC.

International application deadlines are earlier than domestic deadlines and may vary by intake. Intakes can fill before the deadline, so applying early is recommended.

[View the program’s international applicant and entrance information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the listed entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**.

For the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, applicants must complete the pre-entry assessment, meet the English requirement, and satisfy **one** entry option. Qualified applicants are accepted on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**, so intakes may fill before the deadline.

For international applicants, a valid BCIT study permit is also required before starting. Confirm your situation with BCIT Program Advising.

[Review the program’s admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
Which details need human confirmation?

For the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, these details require confirmation with BCIT or the relevant authority:

- **Pre-entry assessment:** The program area must evaluate your work experience, identify any required pre-entry courses, and approve your Proposed Program of Study.
- **English equivalency:** Whether your English qualification meets **Category 2 — English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**.
- **Entry-option equivalency:** Whether your diploma is considered a related, nationally accredited engineering technology credential and whether your course average qualifies.

rule_sets.notes: Find out more about getting started in the program! If the Bachelor of Technology in Electronics program interests you, review the entrance requirements below. If you have any questions regarding the entrance requirements and equivalents, please contact Program Advising . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Courses

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Technology in Electronics is a baccalaureate degree designed for electronics technologists (or equivalent) who wish to complete a degree while working and gain skills for job promotion. The program provides graduates with the knowledge and skills required to design electrical, computer, automation and communication systems. Delivery: in person. See details . About the program The program is approved by the BC Provincial Ministry of Advanced Education. It develops strong mathematics, physics and analytical foundations and broadens this skill set by including business management and liberal studies elements. This degree enhances career advancement opportunities for graduates and supplies the high technology sector with well educated professionals possessing strong practical skills. For projected BTech Electronics course offering information, please view the Course Plan [PDF] and the sample Program Plan [PDF] . You can also take a look at our tentative Fall 202630 Timetable [PDF] . Who it’s for This BCIT Flexible Learning (formerly Part-time Studies) program is scheduled to serve the needs of working professionals who wish to continue their education while working. BCIT Flexible Learning classes are offered year-round, three terms per year, on evenings or weekends. What grads can do B.Tech Electronics graduates have a wide range of career opportunities. They can work as technical design engineers, engineering managers, or professional engineers. They may also join engineering consultancies, pursue careers in sales and marketing, work for the government, become technology entrepreneurs, or further their education with advanced degrees in engineering or business management. conversation.content: Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the listed entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**.

For the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, applicants must complete the pre-entry assessment, meet the English requirement, and satisfy **one** entry option. Qualified applicants are accepted on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**, so intakes may fill before the deadline.

For international applicants, a valid BCIT study permit is also required before starting. Confirm your situation with BCIT Program Advising.

[Review the program’s admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
Which details need human confirmation?

For the **Bachelor of Technology in Electronics**, these details require confirmation with BCIT or the relevant authority:

- **Pre-entry assessment:** The program area must evaluate your work experience, identify any required pre-entry courses, and approve your Proposed Program of Study.
- **English equivalency:** Whether your English qualification meets **Category 2 — English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**.
- **Entry-option equivalency:** Whether your diploma is considered a related, nationally accredited engineering technology credential and whether your course average qualifies.
- **The 60–65% diploma-average route:** Whether your results satisfy the requirement to complete three of the four specified courses—**ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**, **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**, **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**, and **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**—with an overall average of at least 70%.
- **Equivalent education or professional registration:** Whether your education and **ASTTBC** registration, or eligibility to register, satisfy the fourth entry option.
- **International credential evaluation:** Whether an ICES report is required in your circumstances and whether an evaluation from another Canadian service will be accepted.
- **Study permit and international enrolment details:** The program record requires a valid BCIT study permit before starting, but the international source evidence does not publish a definitive study-permit status. Confirm this directly with BCIT.
- **Admission and space:** Meeting the requirements does not guarantee admission; acceptance is first-qualified while space remains, and intakes may fill early.
- **Post-graduation work permit:** The program record says graduates may apply, but final eligibility and approval must be confirmed with **IRCC**.

The best starting point is the program’s admissions information:  
https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/
Can you put that more simply?

Simply put, BCIT needs to confirm:

- Whether your **pre-entry assessment** is complete and whether you need any additional courses.
- Whether your English qualification meets the required standard.
- Whether your diploma qualifies under one of the entry options.
- If using the 60–65% diploma-average option, whether you meet the requirements involving three of these courses:
  - **ELEX 7010 — Engineering Statistics**
  - **ELEX 7020 — Multivariable Calculus and Dynamic Systems**
  - **ELEX 7030 — Thermodynamics**
  - **ELEX 7040 — Engineering Materials**
- Whether your education and **ASTTBC** registration—or eligibility for registration—meet the fourth option.
- Whether your international credential evaluation will be accepted.
- Your study-permit and enrolment details, if you are an international applicant.
- Whether space remains in the intake. Meeting the requirements does **not** guarantee admission.
- Whether you qualify for a post-graduation work permit; final approval comes from **IRCC**.

For confirmation, contact **BCIT Program Advising** and review the [program admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).
And where is it taught again?
Campus: **Burnaby Campus** — 3700 Willingdon Avenue, Burnaby, BC V5G 3H2.
What is the official program link?
Official program link: [Bachelor of Technology in Electronics](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/electronics-bachelor-of-technology-part-time-8900btech/).

rule_sets.name: Electronics BTech admission
rule_sets.notes: Find out more about getting started in the program! If the Bachelor of Technology in Electronics program interests you, review the entrance requirements below. If you have any questions regarding the entrance requirements and equivalents, please contact Program Advising . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants that feel they meet the entrance requirements are required to contact the program head for an evaluation of work experience, assessment for pre-entry courses, and have the Proposed Program of Study form for Technical Coursework approved. Contact the program assistant at 604-432-8237 or soepts@bcit.ca for more information. Any required pre-entry courses that are part of the degree program matrix will be credited towards the degree. You can apply if you have had the pre-entry assessment and have completed any necessary pre-entry courses. A completed pre-entry assessment document from the program area must be uploaded to complete your application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: BCIT diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 2: Diploma from any nationally accredited program in a related engineering technology discipline, with a minimum course average of 65% or Option 3: Students with a diploma grade point average between 60 and 65% can only gain full admission status after completing three of the following courses: ELEX 7010 , ELEX 7020 , ELEX 7030 and ELEX 7040 , with an overall average of 70% or more or Option 4: An equivalent level of education at the post-secondary level and registration (or qualifying to register) as an Applied Science Technologist will be considered. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements A minimum of two years of relevant work experience prior to graduation. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Technology in Electronics is a baccalaureate degree designed for electronics technologists (or equivalent) who wish to complete a degree while working and gain skills for job promotion. The program provides graduates with the knowledge and skills required to design electrical, computer, automation and communication systems. Delivery: in person. See details . About the program The program is approved by the BC Provincial Ministry of Advanced Education. It develops strong mathematics, physics and analytical foundations and broadens this skill set by including business management and liberal studies elements. This degree enhances career advancement opportunities for graduates and supplies the high technology sector with well educated professionals possessing strong practical skills. For projected BTech Electronics course offering information, please view the Course Plan [PDF] and the sample Program Plan [PDF] . You can also take a look at our tentative Fall 202630 Timetable [PDF] . Who it’s for This BCIT Flexible Learning (formerly Part-time Studies) program is scheduled to serve the needs of working professionals who wish to continue their education while working. BCIT Flexible Learning classes are offered year-round, three terms per year, on evenings or weekends. What grads can do B.Tech Electronics graduates have a wide range of career opportunities. They can work as technical design engineers, engineering managers, or professional engineers. They may also join engineering consultancies, pursue careers in sales and marketing, work for the government, become technology entrepreneurs, or further their education with advanced degrees in engineering or business management. Next up Entrance Requirements
